blocks.text: Enzymes are classified on the basis of the reactions they catalyse and also on the basis of the substrates they use.
Classification on the basis of reactions
According to the general type of reaction, enzymes are classified into six classes.

items: Oxidoreductases catalyse the oxidation or reduction of their substrates, adding or removing H+ ions or electrons. For example, cytochrome oxidase catalyses the oxidation of cytochrome.

Transferases catalyse the transfer of a specific functional group (for example methyl, acyl, amino or phosphate) from one substrate to another. For example, hexokinase transfers a phosphate group from ATP to glucose.

Hydrolases catalyse hydrolysis reactions, breaking their substrates into monomers by adding water. For example, lipase, amylase, peptidase and the other digestive enzymes catalyse the hydrolysis of food molecules.
Lyases catalyse the non-hydrolytic addition or removal of groups (for example CO2 or NH2) from substrates. For example, pyruvate decarboxylase removes CO2 from pyruvic acid.
Isomerases catalyse intramolecular rearrangement, converting one isomer into another. For example, hexose isomerase converts glucose to fructose.
Ligases catalyse reactions in which two molecules join by forming new C-C, C-N, C-O or C-S bonds, using energy from ATP. For example, polymerase enzymes join monomers using ATP.

blocks.text: Classification on the basis of substrates

items: Proteases catalyse the breakdown of proteins. Pepsin and trypsin break large polypeptides into smaller polypeptides; aminopeptidases break small polypeptides into dipeptides, and erepsin breaks dipeptides into amino acids.
Lipases act on lipids and catalyse their breakdown. Pancreatic lipase hydrolyses lipids into fatty acids and glycerol.

Carbohydrases act on bigger carbohydrates and break them into smaller units. Amylase breaks starch or glycogen into maltose; cellulase breaks cellulose into cellobiose (a disaccharide) or glucose; maltase breaks maltose into glucose, sucrase breaks sucrose into glucose and fructose, and lactase breaks lactose into glucose and galactose.
Nucleases act on nucleic acids and catalyse their breakdown. RNAase, DNAase and ATPase break down RNA, DNA and ATP respectively.

blocks.prompt: Place each enzyme in its reaction class: hexokinase, lipase, pyruvate decarboxylase, cytochrome oxidase, hexose isomerase, DNA polymerase. Then say which substrate group lipase and amylase belong to.
blocks.explanation: Hexokinase: transferase. Lipase: hydrolase. Pyruvate decarboxylase: lyase. Cytochrome oxidase: oxidoreductase. Hexose isomerase: isomerase. DNA polymerase: ligase. By substrate, lipase is a lipase (acts on lipids) and amylase is a carbohydrase.

items: By reaction, six classes: oxidoreductases (cytochrome oxidase), transferases (hexokinase), hydrolases (digestive enzymes), lyases (pyruvate decarboxylase), isomerases (hexose isomerase), ligases (polymerases, using ATP).
By substrate: proteases (pepsin, trypsin, aminopeptidases, erepsin), lipases (pancreatic lipase), carbohydrases (amylase, cellulase, maltase, sucrase, lactase), nucleases (RNAase, DNAase, ATPase).
